7.0 DATA FLOW

7.1 Context diagram

[[REF context_dfd]] shows Sketchpad as a single process and everything outside it. The owner gives commands and receives drawings, lists and reports. The file system holds the library and saved documents. VS Code edits files directly; the change reaches Sketchpad through the file system, not through Sketchpad. A foreign script enters by import. The printer receives a true-scale template.

[[FIG context_dfd | Context diagram (Level 0)]]

7.2 Level 1: the seven processes

[[REF level1_dfd]] expands process 0. Two flows deserve attention. First, process 2.0 is the only process that writes the open document (D2); every other process reads it. Second, process 1.0 learns of new files from the library folders (D1) directly, by watching them, which is what makes a saved file appear without a Rebuild.

[[FIG level1_dfd | Level 1 data flow diagram]]
ProcessTakesGivesModules
1.0 Maintain catalogfile changes from D1the index (D5); item listsCatalog, Node watcher
2.0 Edit documentcommands; selection and mode from D4the edited document (D2); snapshots (D3)Interaction, Commands, History, Session
3.0 Evaluate geometrythe document (D2)geometryEvaluator, Kernel, Generators
4.0 Rendergeometry; view options (D4); recorded geometrypicture; template fileRenderers
5.0 Host scriptsscript coderecorded geometry or pixels; recording and reportScript host
6.0 Ingest scriptrecording and report; the owner's approvaladapted script (D1)Importer
7.0 Store and retrievesave and open requestsfiles (D1); opened document (D2)Storage, Node service

7.3 Level 2: process 2.0, Edit document

A gesture is interpreted against the session (what is selected, which mode), turned into an intent, then a command. The snapshot is taken before the command is applied, so undo can always return to the state before it. The changed document goes on to evaluation. Undo and redo exchange the open document with a snapshot from history.

[[FIG edit_dfd | Level 2: Edit document]]

7.4 Level 2: process 3.0, Evaluate geometry

Layers are taken in dependency order (Figure 11). For each layer, its handles' point numbers are resolved: free points are read from the table, attached points are computed from paths of layers already finished. The generator's recipe makes the paths, shapers shape them, connectors join them into stitches, and finders name the points that later layers and the nail list need. The loop from 3.6 back to 3.2 is how one layer's named points become available to the next.

[[FIG eval_dfd | Level 2: Evaluate geometry]]

8.0 DATA DICTIONARY

DeMarco notation (Section 1.4). Names in capitals are defined elsewhere in this dictionary.

DOCUMENT        = format + title + units + (scale) + POINT-TABLE + {LAYER} + layerOrder + OUTPUT-SETTINGS
format          = * whole number; 2 for the first V2 format *
units           = [ "mm" | "in" | "legacy" ]
POINT-TABLE     = {pointNumber + POINT}
pointNumber     = * whole number, permanent, never reused *
POINT           = [ FREE-POINT | ATTACHED-POINT ]
FREE-POINT      = x + y
ATTACHED-POINT  = on + [ t | feature ]
on              = * a layerId *
t               = * fraction along the path, 0 to 1 *
feature         = * a finder's name, e.g. "tip of lobe 3" *
LAYER           = layerId + legacyNumber + [ GENERATOR-USE | DOCUMENT-REF ] + transform + role
                  + identityColor + includeInOutput
GENERATOR-USE   = generatorId + generatorVersion + {setting} + {handleName + pointNumber}
DOCUMENT-REF    = documentPath + [ "reference" | "copy" ]
role            = [ "stitch" | "guide" | "scaffold" | "image" ]
transform       = angle + tx + ty
OUTPUT-SETTINGS = (nailDiameter) + (clearance) + (paper) + (tiling) + (labels)

SESSION         = {tabId + TAB-SESSION}
TAB-SESSION     = {openDocument} + activeLayer + mode + showAll + {hiddenLayer} + (selectedPoint) + zoom + pan
HISTORY         = {SNAPSHOT} + position + savedPosition
SNAPSHOT        = commandName + DOCUMENT

GENERATOR-FILE  = META + PARAMS + [ build | run ] + (drag) + (migrate)
META            = id + version + title + {tag} + notes
PARAMS          = {settingName + SETTING-DEF}
SETTING-DEF     = type + default + (min) + (max) + (step) + (label) + (widget) + (section) + (showIf) + (handle)
type            = [ "int" | "number" | "angle" | "color" | "choice" | "bool" | "text" | "point" | "points" | "pathRef" ]

PATH            = {point} + closed
GEOMETRY        = {pathName + PATH} + {STITCH} + {pointName + point} + bounds + style
STITCH          = point + point

CATALOG-ENTRY   = itemId + kind + category + title + status + sourcePath + (thumbnail) + (report) + (badge)
kind            = [ "generator" | "script" | "legacyScript" | "foreignScript" | "document" | "image" ]
ITEM-METADATA   = status + {tag} + (order) + (hidden)       * the small file beside each item *
SCRIPT-REPORT   = {STITCH-GUESS} + {SETTING-GUESS} + {globalTouched} + usesNetwork + animates + runTime

An example document, to show that a figure can be read and understood in VS Code:

{ "format": 2, "title": "Two parabolas", "units": "mm", "scale": 0.5,
  "points": { "9": [60, 30], "10": [60, 190], "11": [220, 190],
              "14": { "on": "L3", "t": 0.25 } },
  "layers": [
    { "id": "L1", "n": 1, "use": "parabola@1", "role": "stitch",
      "settings": { "steps": 18, "color": "#0044cc" },
      "handles":  { "a": 9, "b1": 10, "b2": 10, "c": 11 } },
    { "id": "L2", "n": 2, "doc": "figures/stars/smallStar.json", "mode": "reference",
      "transform": { "angle": 30, "tx": 200, "ty": 0 } }
  ],
  "order": ["L2", "L1"] }

9.0 CHANGES FROM VERSION 1

AreaVersion 1Version 2Solves
GeometryExists while painting; draw() and infrastructure() must agreebuild() returns all geometry as data, onceP-1
ObjectsShared singletons with live settings; Object.create copiesGenerators hold no state; each layer has its own settings in the documentP-2
Settingsparams with a points[] mirror and derived values, all savedSettings only; handles name point numbers; nothing derived is savedP-3
Draggingupdate() guesses which handle movedA drag writes one named setting or point through a commandP-4
HandlesUndeclared; found by coordinate matchingDeclared by name and role; drag() for unusual onesP-5
WeldsGroups of copies kept in step by a propagation walkShared point numbers and one-way attachments; evaluation in orderP-6
UndoNoneSnapshot history; one gesture, one stepP-7
StateOne object per tab mixing three kindsDocument, session and interaction kept apartP-8
Tab switchingDecision order of flagsClose, then open from own stateP-9
ListsStored manifests, rebuilt and checkedIndex worked out from folders plus a metadata file per itemP-10
Files and NodeTwo boundaries, often bypassedOne Storage module, checked automaticallyP-11
ScriptsShared globals and stateIsolated frame, fresh canvas per runP-12
Adding itemsRestart or Rebuild; registry list edited by handSave the file; it appearsP-13
ControlsTwo blocks; widget names; aliases; widgets write settingsOne typed schema; widgets send commandsP-14
OutputCanvas pixels; no true-scale printUnits, SVG, calibrated PDF, nail list, spacing checkP-15
Menus, wordsEight menu files; "overlay" three waysOne commands table; panel and canvas layerP-16
MetadataSeven unread fields; decorative versionOnly fields that are read; version drives migrationP-17
ParametricsSeparate code; spacing tools for ellipses onlyA maker like any other; shapers work on every pathP-18
Adapting scriptsBy hand, into a second formatImporter proposes levels 1 to 3; owner approvesP-19

What is retired. drawState.js globals; window.drawRegistry and its hand-kept list; manifests as authority, maintain_manifests, the start-up rebuild and the Home alert bar's reason for existing; fileLayer and direct nodeDispatch calls; the weld propagation walk and cornerPartners(); needsUpdate; the per-tab menu files; TinyMCE.

What is kept, by intent. The six tabs; Notes from header comments; permanent ids; stable numbers; layer transforms; infrastructure (now paths); the list builder's isolation; the playpen rule; the local Node service and its path safety; plain JavaScript.
